### 🟡 Off-by-one in array bounds check allows index equal to length

The guard uses `index > values.length`, but valid nonnegative indices for an array of length n are 0 through n-1. Because of the strict greater-than, `at(values, values.length)` passes the guard and returns `values[values.length]`, which is `undefined`, instead of throwing RangeError as the JSDoc promises.

**Evidence:** `if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0 || index > values.length)` permits index === values.length, so `return values[index]` yields undefined for that value.

**Suggested change:**

Change the comparison to `index >= values.length`.

<sub>correctness · confidence 95%</sub>
